예레미야-4-2.title: 예레미야 4장 2절 역사문법적 주해
예레미야-4-2.exegesis: CHAPTER 4 Jr 4:1-31 . Continuation of Address to the Ten Tribes of Israel. ( Jr 4:1 , 2 ). The Prophet Turns Again to Judah, to Whom He Had Originally Been Sent ( Jr 4:3-31 ). 1. return ... return-- play on words. "If thou wouldest return to thy land (thou must first), return (by conversion and repentance) to Me." not remove-- no longer be an unsettled wanderer in a strange land. So Cain ( Ge 4:12 , 14 ).

예레미야-4-3.title: 예레미야 4장 3절 역사문법적 주해
예레미야-4-3.exegesis: 2. And thou-- rather, "And if (carried on from Jr 4:1 ) thou shalt swear, 'Jehovah liveth,' in truth, &c.", that is, if thou shalt worship Him (for we swear by the God whom we worship; compare De 6:13 ; 10:20 ; Is 19:18 ; Am 8:14 ) in sincerity, &c. and the nations-- Rather, this is apodosis to the "if"; then shall the nations bless themselves in (by) Him" ( Is 65:16 ). The conversion of the nations will be the consequence of Israel's conversion ( Psa 102:13 , 15 ; Ro 11:12 , 15 ).

예레미야-4-4.title: 예레미야 4장 4절 역사문법적 주해
예레미야-4-4.exegesis: 3. Transition to Judah. Supply mentally. All which (the foregoing declaration as to Israel) applies to Judah. and Jerusalem-- that is, and especially the men of Jerusalem, as being the most prominent in Judea. Break ... fallow ground-- that is, Repent of your idolatry, and so be prepared to serve the Lord in truth ( Ho 10:12 ; Mt 13:7 ). The unhumbled heart is like ground which may be improved, being let out to us for that purpose, but which is as yet fallow, overgrown with weeds, its natural product.

예레미야-4-5.exegesis: 4. Remove your natural corruption of heart ( De 10:16 ; 30:6 ; Ro 2:29 ; Col 2:11 ).

예레미야-4-6.title: 예레미야 4장 6절 역사문법적 주해
예레미야-4-6.exegesis: 5. cry, gather together-- rather, "cry fully" that is, loudly. The Jews are warned to take measures against the impending Chaldean invasion (compare Jr 8:14 ).
예레미야-4-6.theologicalNote: 5. cry, gather together-- rather, "cry fully" that is, loudly. The Jews are warned to take measures against the impending Chaldean invasion (compare Jr 8:14 ).

예레미야-4-7.title: 예레미야 4장 7절 역사문법적 주해
예레미야-4-7.exegesis: 6. Zion-- The standard toward Zion intimated that the people of the surrounding country were to fly to it, as being the strongest of their fortresses.

예레미야-4-8.exegesis: 7. lion-- Nebuchadnezzar and the Chaldeans ( Jr 2:15 ; 5:6 ; Da 7:14 ). his thicket-- lair; Babylon. destroyer of the Gentiles-- rather, "the nations" ( Jr 25:9 ).

예레미야-4-9.title: 예레미야 4장 9절 역사문법적 주해
예레미야-4-9.exegesis: 8. Nothing is left to the Jews but to bewail their desperate condition. anger ... not turned back-- ( Is 9:12 , 17, 21).
예레미야-4-9.theologicalNote: 8. Nothing is left to the Jews but to bewail their desperate condition. anger ... not turned back-- ( Is 9:12 , 17, 21).

예레미야-4-10.title: 예레미야 4장 10절 역사문법적 주해
예레미야-4-10.exegesis: 9. heart-- The wisdom of the most leading men will be utterly at a loss to devise means of relief.
예레미야-4-10.theologicalNote: 9. heart-- The wisdom of the most leading men will be utterly at a loss to devise means of relief.

예레미야-4-11.title: 예레미야 4장 11절 역사문법적 주해
예레미야-4-11.exegesis: 10. thou hast ... deceived-- God, having even the false prophets in His hands, is here said to do that which for inscrutable purposes He permits them to do ( Ex 9:12 ; 2Th 2:11 ; compare Jr 8:15 ; which passage shows that the dupes of error were self-prepared for it, and that God's predestination did not destroy their moral freedom as voluntary agents). The false prophets foretold "peace," and the Jews believed them; God overruled this to His purposes ( Jr 5:12 ; 14:13 ; Eze 14:9 ). soul-- rather, "reacheth to the life."

예레미야-4-12.title: 예레미야 4장 12절 역사문법적 주해
예레미야-4-12.exegesis: 11. dry wind-- the simoom, terrific and destructive, blowing from the southeast across the sandy deserts east of Palestine. Image of the invading Babylonian army ( Ho 13:15 ). Babylon in its turn shall be visited by a similar "destroying wind" ( Jr 51:1 ). of ... high places-- that is, that sweeps over the high places. daughter-- that is, the children of my people. not to fan-- a very different wind from those ordinary winds employed for fanning the grain in the open air.

예레미야-4-13.exegesis: 12. full ... from those places-- rather, "a wind fuller (that is, more impetuous) than those winds" (which fan the corn) ( Jr 4:11 ) [Rosenmuller]. unto me-- "for Me," as My instrument for executing My purpose. sentence-- judgments against them ( Jr 1:16 ).

예레미야-4-14.title: 예레미야 4장 14절 역사문법적 주해
예레미야-4-14.exegesis: 13. clouds-- continuing the metaphor in Jr 4:11 : 12 . Clouds of sand and dust accompany the simoom, and after rapid gyrations ascend like a pillar. eagles-- ( De 28:49 ; Ha 1:8 ). Woe unto us-- The people are graphically presented before us, without it being formally so stated, bursting out in these exclamations.

예레미야-4-15.title: 예레미야 4장 15절 역사문법적 주해
예레미야-4-15.exegesis: 14. Only one means of deliverance is left to the Jews-- a thorough repentance. vain thoughts-- namely, projects for deliverance, such as enlisting the Egyptians on their side. Gesenius translates, "How long wilt thou harbor vain thoughts?"

예레미야-4-16.title: 예레미야 4장 16절 역사문법적 주해
예레미야-4-16.exegesis: 15. For ... from Dan-- The connection is: There is danger in delay; for the voice of a messenger announces the approach of the Chaldean enemy from Dan, the northern frontier of Palestine ( Jr 8:16 ; compare Jr 4:6 ; Jr 1:14 ). Mount Ephraim-- which borders closely on Judah; so that the foe is coming nearer and nearer. Dan and Beth-el in Ephraim were the two places where Jeroboam set up the idolatrous calves ( 1Ki 12:29 ); just retribution.

예레미야-4-17.exegesis: 16. The neighboring foreign "nations" are summoned to witness Jehovah's judgments on His rebel people ( Jr 6:18 , 19 ). watchers-- that is, besiegers (compare 2Sa 11:16 ); observed or watched, that is, besieged. their voice-- the war shout.

예레미야-4-19.exegesis: 18. ( Jr 2:17 , 19; Psa 107:17 ). this is thy wickedness-- that is, the fruit of thy wickedness.
예레미야-4-19.theologicalNote: 18. ( Jr 2:17 , 19; Psa 107:17 ). this is thy wickedness-- that is, the fruit of thy wickedness.

예레미야-4-20.title: 예레미야 4장 20절 역사문법적 주해
예레미야-4-20.exegesis: 19. The prophet suddenly assumes the language of the Jewish state personified, lamenting its affliction ( Jr 10:19 , 20 ; 9:1 , 10 ; Is 15:5 ; compare Lu 19:41 ). at my very heart-- Hebrew, "at the walls of my heart"; the muscles round the heart. There is a climax, the "bowels," the pericardium, the "heart" itself. maketh ... noise-- moaneth [Henderson]. alarm-- the battle shout.

예레미야-4-21.exegesis: 20. Destruction ... cried-- Breach upon breach is announced ( Psa 42:7 ; Eze 7:26 ). The war "trumpet" ... the battle shout ... the "destructions" ... the havoc throughout "the whole land" ... the spoiling of the shepherds' "tents" ( Jr 10:20 ; or, "tents" means cities, which should be overthrown as easily as tents [Calvin]), form a gradation.

예레미야-4-22.exegesis: 21. Judah in perplexity asks, How long is this state of things to continue?
예레미야-4-22.theologicalNote: 21. Judah in perplexity asks, How long is this state of things to continue?

예레미야-4-23.title: 예레미야 4장 23절 역사문법적 주해
예레미야-4-23.exegesis: 22. Jehovah's reply; they cannot be otherwise than miserable, since they persevere in sin. The repetition of clauses gives greater force to the sentiment. wise ... evil ... to do good ... no knowledge-- reversing the rule ( Ro 16:19 ) "wise unto ... good, simple concerning evil."

예레미야-4-24.title: 예레미야 4장 24절 역사문법적 주해
예레미야-4-24.exegesis: 23. Graphic picture of the utter desolation about to visit Palestine. "I beheld, and lo!" four times solemnly repeated, heightens the awful effect of the scene (compare Is 24:19 ; 34:11 ). without form and void-- reduced to the primeval chaos ( Ge 1:2 ).

예레미야-4-25.exegesis: 24. mountains-- ( Is 5:25 ). moved lightly-- shook vehemently.
예레미야-4-25.theologicalNote: 24. mountains-- ( Is 5:25 ). moved lightly-- shook vehemently.

예레미야-4-26.title: 예레미야 4장 26절 역사문법적 주해
예레미야-4-26.exegesis: 25. no man ... birds-- No vestige of the human, or of the feathered creation, is to be seen ( Eze 38:20 ; Zep 1:3 ).
예레미야-4-26.theologicalNote: 25. no man ... birds-- No vestige of the human, or of the feathered creation, is to be seen ( Eze 38:20 ; Zep 1:3 ).

예레미야-4-27.title: 예레미야 4장 27절 역사문법적 주해
예레미야-4-27.exegesis: 26. fruitful place-- Hebrew, Carmel. a wilderness-- Hebrew, "the wilderness," in contrast to "the fruitful place"; the great desert, where Carmel was, there is now the desert of Arabia [Maurer]. cities-- in contrast to the fruitful place or field.

예레미야-4-28.title: 예레미야 4장 28절 역사문법적 주해
예레미야-4-28.exegesis: 27. full end-- utter destruction: I will leave some hope of restoration ( Jr 5:10 , 18 ; 30:11 ; 46:28 ; compare Le 26:44 ).
예레미야-4-28.theologicalNote: 27. full end-- utter destruction: I will leave some hope of restoration ( Jr 5:10 , 18 ; 30:11 ; 46:28 ; compare Le 26:44 ).

예레미야-4-29.title: 예레미야 4장 29절 역사문법적 주해
예레미야-4-29.exegesis: 28. For this-- on account of the desolations just described ( Is 5:30 ; Ho 4:3 ). not repent-- ( Nu 23:19 ).
예레미야-4-29.theologicalNote: 28. For this-- on account of the desolations just described ( Is 5:30 ; Ho 4:3 ). not repent-- ( Nu 23:19 ).

예레미야-4-30.title: 예레미야 4장 30절 역사문법적 주해
예레미야-4-30.exegesis: 29. whole city-- Jerusalem: to it the inhabitants of the country had fled for refuge; but when it, too, is likely to fall, they flee out of it to hide in the "thickets." Henderson translates, "every city." noise-- The mere noise of the hostile horsemen shall put you to flight.

예레미야-4-31.title: 예레미야 4장 31절 역사문법적 주해
예레미야-4-31.exegesis: 30. when thou art spoiled-- rather, "thou, O destroyed one" [Maurer]. rentest ... face with painting-- Oriental women paint their eyes with stibium, or antimony, to make them look full and sparkling, the black margin causing the white of the eyes to appear the brighter by contrast ( 2Ki 9:30 ). He uses the term "distendest" in derision of their effort to make their eyes look large [Maurer]; or else, "rentest," that is, dost lacerate by puncturing the eyelid in order to make the antimony adhere [Rosenmuller]. So the Jews use every artifice to secure the aid of Egypt against Babylon. face-- rather, thy eyes ( Eze 23:40 ).
